intent: Increased sensor size to 0.016 and spread sensors wider to ±0.05 m for better line coverage and detection robustness, especially on complex tracks. Increased base speed to 1.2 to test higher speed capability while monitoring control stability. Expect improved line loss performance and higher overall score.
rationale: The integration feedback praises the current geometry for its stable platform and well-spaced sensors that cover the tape line effectively. The controller uses a smooth gradient of sensor weights, indicating good sensor placement. The race data shows a perfect finish on the oval track with no line loss and very low error, but the s-bend track run ended off-track with one line loss event and higher error, suggesting room for improvement in sensor coverage and speed control. To improve robustness and coverage, I will increase the sensor size from 0.012 to 0.016 to enhance line detection. I will also spread the sensors slightly wider from ±0.04 m to ±0.05 m to cover a broader area, which should help in sharper curves like the s-bend. Additionally, I will increase the base speed from 1.0 (default) to 1.2 to test higher speed capability, expecting the integrator to adjust control gains accordingly. I keep the wheel track, wheel radius, body dimensions, and mass unchanged to maintain stability and inertia balance. I expect these changes to improve line detection robustness and coverage, reduce line loss on complex tracks, and increase overall speed and score. I request measurements of completion, progress, line_loss_events, rms_error, and completion_time to evaluate these effects.
